description: Learn form elements, inputs, buttons, and client-side validation.

slides.title: Introduction to HTML Forms
slides.content:
# HTML Forms & User Input 📝

Forms are the backbone of interactivity on the web. They collect data from users—such as credentials, search terms, payments, and feedback—and transmit it to servers.

## What you'll master:
- 📋 **The `<form>` Element** - Action, method, and encoding types
- ⌨️ **Input Controls** - Text, password, email, numbers, dates, and checkboxes
- 🔘 **Buttons & Submission** - Submit, reset, and custom buttons
- 🏷️ **Accessible Labelling** - Form accessibility with `<label>` and `<fieldset>`
- 🛡️ **HTML5 Validation** - Client-side validation without writing complex code

slides.title: The <form> Element Attributes
slides.content:
# The `<form>` Element Attributes ⚙️

The `<form>` element acts as a container for all interactive input controls.

```html_not
<form action="/api/register" method="POST" autocomplete="on">
  <!-- Input controls go here -->
</form>
```

## Critical Attributes:
1. **`action`**: The destination URL where form data is sent upon submission.
2. **`method`**: The HTTP method used (`GET` or `POST`).
   - `GET`: Appends data to the URL as query parameters (`?query=code`). Good for searches.
   - `POST`: Sends data in the HTTP request body. Mandatory for passwords and sensitive data.
3. **`enctype`**: Specifies encoding type. Use `multipart/form-data` when uploading files!

slides.title: Labels and Accessibility
slides.content:
# Form Labels (`<label>`) 🏷️

Every input field must have an associated `<label>` for accessibility and usability.

## Two Ways to Associate Labels:

### 1. Explicit Association with `for` (Recommended):
```html_not
<label for="user-email">Email Address:</label>
<input type="email" id="user-email" name="email">
```
*(The `for` attribute on the label must match the `id` of the input).*

### 2. Implicit Nesting:
```html_not
<label>
  Username:
  <input type="text" name="username">
</label>
```

> 💡 **User Experience Perk:** Clicking the label automatically focuses or toggles the associated input control!

slides.title: Text and Password Inputs
slides.content:
# Text & Password Inputs 🔑

The `<input>` tag is the most versatile form element. Its behavior changes based on the `type` attribute.

```html_not
<label for="fname">First Name:</label>
<input type="text" id="fname" name="firstname" placeholder="Jane" maxlength="30">

<label for="pwd">Password:</label>
<input type="password" id="pwd" name="password" placeholder="••••••••">
```

## Common Attributes:
- `name`: The parameter key sent in the HTTP request payload.
- `placeholder`: Temporary hint text visible before user enters input.
- `value`: Initial or current value of the field.
- `readonly`: Prevents editing while still submitting the field.
- `disabled`: Disables input and prevents it from submitting.

slides.title: Modern HTML5 Input Types
slides.content:
# Modern HTML5 Input Types 📱

HTML5 introduced specialized input types that provide native validation and customized mobile keyboards.

```html_not
<!-- Triggers mobile numeric keypad -->
<input type="tel" name="phone" placeholder="+1 (555) 000-0000">

<!-- Validates email structure & shows @ on mobile keyboard -->
<input type="email" name="user_email" required>

<!-- Validates numeric range -->
<input type="number" name="quantity" min="1" max="100" step="1">

<!-- Native URL formatting check -->
<input type="url" name="portfolio" placeholder="https://example.com">
```

> 📱 **Mobile Keyboards:** On smartphones, `<input type="email">` automatically shows the `@` and `.com` keys, while `<input type="number">` brings up the numeric pad!

slides.title: Date, Time, and Color Pickers
slides.content:
# Pickers: Date, Time & Color 📅

Modern browsers render built-in interactive widgets for dates, times, and colors.

```html_not
<!-- Date picker calendar -->
<label for="bday">Birthday:</label>
<input type="date" id="bday" name="birthday" min="1900-01-01" max="2026-12-31">

<!-- Time picker -->
<label for="meeting">Meeting Time:</label>
<input type="time" id="meeting" name="meeting_time">

<!-- Color picker widget -->
<label for="theme">Choose Brand Color:</label>
<input type="color" id="theme" name="theme_color" value="#3b82f6">
```

slides.title: Dropdowns with <select>
slides.content:
# Dropdown Menus with `<select>` 🔽

The `<select>` element creates a dropdown list of options.

```html_not
<label for="country">Country:</label>
<select id="country" name="country">
  <optgroup label="North America">
    <option value="us">United States</option>
    <option value="ca">Canada</option>
  </optgroup>
  <optgroup label="Europe">
    <option value="uk" selected>United Kingdom</option>
    <option value="de">Germany</option>
  </optgroup>
</select>
```

- `<option>`: Defines each selectable item (`value` is sent to server).
- `<optgroup>`: Groups related options with a category label.
- `selected`: Attribute to set the default active choice.

slides.title: Autocomplete with <datalist>
slides.content:
# Suggestions with `<datalist>` 💡

The `<datalist>` element provides an auto-complete suggestion list while still allowing users to enter custom text.

```html_not
<label for="browser-choice">Choose a Browser:</label>
<input list="browsers" id="browser-choice" name="browser">

<datalist id="browsers">
  <option value="Chrome">
  <option value="Firefox">
  <option value="Safari">
  <option value="Edge">
  <option value="Brave">
</datalist>
```

## How It Works:
The `list` attribute on the `<input>` must match the `id` of the `<datalist>`. As the user types, matching suggestions appear!

slides.title: Multi-Line Text with <textarea>
slides.content:
# Multi-Line Text with `<textarea>` 📄

For multi-line inputs such as comments, feedback, or messages, use the `<textarea>` element.

```html_not
<label for="bio">Biography:</label>
<textarea id="bio" name="user_bio" rows="4" cols="50" placeholder="Tell us about yourself..."></textarea>
```

## Crucial `<textarea>` Details:
- Unlike `<input>`, `<textarea>` has both an opening and closing tag!
- Default content is placed **between** tags: `<textarea>Default text</textarea>`.
- Attributes `rows` and `cols` define initial visible dimensions in text characters (though CSS is usually preferred for sizing).

slides.title: Buttons and Submission
slides.content:
# Buttons and Submission 🔘

Buttons allow users to trigger actions within forms.

```html_not
<!-- 1. Submit Button (default type inside a form) -->
<button type="submit">Submit Registration</button>

<!-- 2. Reset Button (restores form fields to defaults) -->
<button type="reset">Clear Form</button>

<!-- 3. Standard Action Button (controlled by JavaScript) -->
<button type="button" onclick="calculateTotal()">Calculate</button>
```

> ⚠️ **Default Button Warning:** Any `<button>` inside a `<form>` without an explicit `type` attribute defaults to `type="submit"`, which will unexpectedly submit the form when clicked! Always specify `type="button"` for JS buttons.

slides.title: File Uploads with <input type='file'>
slides.content:
# File Uploads with `<input type="file">` 📁

Allow users to upload images, documents, or files.

```html_not
<form action="/upload" method="POST" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <label for="avatar">Upload Profile Picture:</label>
  <input type="file" id="avatar" name="avatar" accept="image/png, image/jpeg" multiple>
  <button type="submit">Upload</button>
</form>
```

## Critical File Upload Rules:
1. `method` **must** be `POST`.
2. `enctype` **must** be set to `multipart/form-data`.
3. `accept` restricts file types (e.g. `image/*`, `.pdf`).
4. `multiple` allows selecting more than one file.

slides.title: HTML5 Native Form Validation
slides.content:
# Native HTML5 Form Validation 🛡️

HTML5 provides automatic client-side validation without needing JavaScript.

```html_not
<form>
  <!-- Required field -->
  <input type="text" name="username" required>
  
  <!-- Min and Max length -->
  <input type="password" name="pwd" minlength="8" maxlength="20" required>
  
  <!-- Number bounds -->
  <input type="number" name="age" min="18" max="99">
  
  <!-- Regex Pattern matching (e.g., 5-digit zip code) -->
  <input type="text" name="zipcode" pattern="[0-9]{5}" title="Enter a 5-digit ZIP code">
  
  <button type="submit">Sign Up</button>
</form>
```

When a user submits with invalid data, the browser prevents submission and displays a localized validation tooltip!

slides.title: Styling Validation with CSS
Hidden Inputs for State
slides.content:
# Hidden Inputs (`type="hidden"`) 🕵️

Hidden inputs store data that users do not need to see or edit, but must be submitted along with the form.

```html_not
<form action="/checkout" method="POST">
  <!-- Hidden metadata -->
  <input type="hidden" name="user_id" value="4821">
  <input type="hidden" name="session_token" value="abc123xyz">
  
  <button type="submit">Complete Purchase</button>
</form>
```

## Typical Use Cases:
- Security tokens (Anti-CSRF tokens)
- Database record IDs
- Analytics tracking parameters
- Multi-step form step counters

slides.title: Form Security Best Practices
slides.content:
# Form Security Best Practices 🔒

Always adhere to these security principles when implementing forms:

1. **Never Trust Client Validation:** HTML5 validation can be bypassed by anyone using DevTools or curl. Always validate thoroughly on the backend server!
2. **Use HTTPS:** Sensitive information (credentials, credit cards) submitted over plaintext HTTP can be intercepted.
3. **Use POST for Modifications:** Never send passwords or create/update resources via `GET` requests.
4. **Implement CSRF Protection:** Use unique anti-CSRF tokens for all state-modifying requests.
5. **Set `autocomplete="off"` for Sensitive Data:** Protect one-time passwords and credit card security codes.

slides.title: Summary & Next Steps
slides.content:
# Forms Mastered! 🌟

You now have complete mastery over user input collection and validation in HTML!

## Key Takeaways:
- ✅ **Form Anatomy:** `<form>` uses `action`, `method="POST"`, and `enctype` for uploads.
- ✅ **Accessibility:** Always link `<label for="id">` to its input.
- ✅ **Input Types:** Utilize `email`, `tel`, `date`, `color`, and `checkbox`.
- ✅ **Radios:** Group radio buttons using identical `name` values.
- ✅ **Validation:** Built-in `required`, `pattern`, `minlength`, and `min`/`max`.
